items.title: Buddy Burns Interview, 1958-08-14
items.q: Chester showed me how to uh, to swing. He showed me the swing part in the deal. Chester's the one who started me out.

ctx.x: Um, can you remember any of the other early bass players that you uh, liked?

Yeah, I liked it uh, I like, I can't call this fella Ellick, his name is Ellick. He's a very good bass player. His last name, I always wished to play bass like him when I grew up. And also uh, also Pop Foster, George Foster. That's another one, I always admired his bass playing. I always wished to play bass like him. And then uh, when I started playing bass, Liv Newton started me off and then I got hooked up with Chester, Chester Zardes. And I know the music some, but I didn't know very much. And Chester showed…
In those days were you using the bow or picking?

items.title: Buddy Burns Interview, 1958-08-14
items.q: he showed me the swing. I had lots of other teachers and things, but he showed me the swing, he did.

ctx.x: Well, I'm gonna tell you. That is the truth. This is Chester. Chester's artist.

That's right. He's about the, he's about the, I would say, about the hardest working boy that I saw play bass. He's just about the hardest worker. I wouldn't say he the best, but that's the one I prefer. That's the one you like. And I play his own order, him, because he showed me the swing. Yeah. He showed me the swing. I had lots of other teachers and things, but he showed me the swing, he did. Yeah. Now, Lev Newton, he was kind of a, he liked it, he didn't like too much of, you know, too much of swinging too…
